events.note: Authored by an AI agent run (issue #114, parent #92) from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted; synthetic values only; not independently reviewed.
Statement 'user-id-public-status' is recorded as unresolved: Whether the user-id portion is public, personal data or part of the secret is not stated.

Decided 2026-10-04 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner), ADR 0019 item 7 (#114), user-id. This case decides its fixture. Question: In a Basic Authorization token, which part is the secret, and what is the cleartext user-id beside it? Options: the whole token is the secret and the user-id is also secret; the password is the secret and the user-id is a companion; or leave open. Decision: The encoded token is the secret span (it carries the password). The cleartext user-id is a companion span, not secret and not a personal-data expectation: credential and personal-data populations stay separate. Reason: The password is the confidential part; RFC 9110 17.16.1 separates the identity effect of a credential from the confidentiality of its content. Project policy, not a provider rule or a fact. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's instruction.
events.dissent: The standard does not say the user-id is public, and a user-id beside a password is half a login; calling it a companion understates it.
events.reversingEvidence: A standard that says the user-id is confidential or public, or a decision that account identifiers are sensitive.
